name: Praxis
language: F# (.NET 10); some Python/shell tooling; F#-first conformant
proposed_responsibility: Governance; verified completion; authenticated provenance/attestation receipts; protected release gates
implemented_capabilities: Work protocol and completion gate (src/Praxis.Domain/Work/CompletionGate.fs); verifier-signed completion receipts: ECDSA P-256 DSSE envelopes, key in memory or PEM (src/Praxis.Infrastructure/Work/TrustedVerifier.fs, src/Praxis.Domain/Work/VerificationReceipt.fs); protected completion policy compared against ros.json at merge base of protected branch, refuses weakening (src/Praxis.Application/Work/ProtectedCompletionPolicy.fs; docs/verified-completion-rollout.md REL-GATE-003/004); ECIR gates and authority (src/Praxis.Infrastructure/Planning/*Ecir*.fs); actor provenance on executions and front matter with re-attribution refusal (src/Praxis.Domain/Provenance/*.fs); remote execution records requester vs observed executor vs transport principal (docs/agent-provenance.md)
test_evidence: tests-executed (partial): dotnet run tests/Praxis.Tests (custom runner, .NET SDK 10.0.404) hit the 10-minute cap (exit 124) before completing; 1303 PASS and 0 FAIL lines observed before timeout; AttestedCompletionTests are last in the suite list and were likely NOT reached - attested-completion behaviour is source-inspected only; 208 test .fs files in repo. (dotnet test on this Exe project runs nothing)
specified_only: Signed events / signed execution records and key management explicitly deferred to an attestation service (docs/agent-provenance.md 'Identity is provenance, not authentication'; DF-ROS-2026-A036); mandatory verified completion NOT enabled across repositories (docs/verified-completion-rollout.md line 3)
missing_capabilities: Authenticated actor identity (provenance is self-reported; 'does not defend against a malicious process that lies about itself'); events.jsonl not signed or hash-chained; protected source is the local git ref (defeatable by a process that rewrites refs/remotes/origin/HEAD); verifier socket unauthenticated; no evidence of branch-protection settings being verified by Praxis itself (Conditor owns that); repo-wide rollout of requireVerifiedCompletion not done
architectural_fit: Strong fit for governance and verified completion; attestation is receipt-level (validation results signed by host verifier), not actor-level
required_extensions: Bind executions to platform identity (GitHub Actions OIDC / GitHub App installation token) and sign execution records; hash-chain or sign events.jsonl; enable requireVerifiedCompletion + trustedVerifierKeyIds in assurance-scoped repos; host-side audit of protected refs; publish receipts to external store (Arca/managed WORM)
alternative_approach: Sigstore/cosign keyless signing with GitHub OIDC and in-toto attestations; GitHub artifact attestations (actions/attest-build-provenance); GitHub rulesets with required status checks for gate enforcement
security_implications: Self-reported provenance must not be presented to auditors as authenticated identity; verifier key in process memory (root on verifier host can read it); unattested mode forgeable by repository writer (documented)
incremental_effort: M (identity binding + event signing); S per repo to enable verified completion

name: Dokimos
language: F# (.NET 8 test projects; global SDK pin); small Python/shell; F#-first conformant
proposed_responsibility: Independent verification of completion claims; quality gates
implemented_capabilities: dokimos completion verify: treats Praxis completion packet as untrusted, checks against host-supplied authority (work item, claim token, fencing generation, commit, Ordo contract digest), evidence matched by ID+SHA-256+revision, replay protection via consumed packet digests, exit codes 0/3/4 (src/Dokimos.Core/CompletionVerification.fs; docs/completion-verification.md); verification of verifier-signed DSSE receipts with pinned keys (src/Dokimos.Core/CompletionAttestation.fs VerifyData); ECIR audit (src/Dokimos.Core/EcirAudit.fs); construction/behaviour verification; quality-gate GitHub Action with SHA-256-pinned package and enforce flag (actions/quality-gate/action.yml); evidence store (src/Dokimos.Core/EvidenceStore.fs)
test_evidence: tests-executed: Dokimos.Domain.Tests 4/4 passed; Dokimos.Core.Tests 436/436 passed; Dokimos.Cli.Tests 157/157 passed (total 597 passed, 0 failed) on .NET SDK 10.0.404 with DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major (projects target net8.0); 80 test .fs files
specified_only: Dokimos' own verification receipt is not signed by Dokimos (only verifies others' signatures; no SignData in src)
missing_capabilities: Independence is logical, not operational: runs as a CLI/Action in the same CI/repo trust domain; Dokimos receipts unsigned; whether a failing gate blocks merge depends on GitHub required checks (not evidenced in-repo); no central receipt store
architectural_fit: Good fit as independent verifier of completion claims; must be operated by a principal separate from the implementing agent to be 'independent'
required_extensions: Sign Dokimos verification receipts (DSSE, same envelope as Praxis); run in a separate workflow/environment with its own identity and key; publish receipts to external evidence store; required-check enforcement verified via Conditor/Tutela
alternative_approach: GitHub required status checks + rulesets; separate GitHub App identity for verifier; SLSA verifier tooling
security_implications: If Dokimos runs with the same token/workspace as the implementer, an agent can influence the authority input; contents: write token in quality-gate persists evidence (scope minimisation needed)
